item.title: Over 90 people waiting for a bed at local hospitals today
item.description: Over 90 people are waiting for a bed at local hospitals today. Sligo University Hospital is the fourth busiest in the country with 53 people on trolleys. Portiuncula University Hospital in Ballinasloe is extremely busy today with 30 people waiting for a bed whilst there are 9 people waiting in Mullingar. Local Fianna Fáil TD Martin Daly says people should contact their local GP before traveling to hospital: Advertisement

item.title: No injuries reported following crash in South Leitrim
item.description: No injuries have been reported following a crash in south Leitrim. Gardaí and emergency services attended the collision which occurred on the R209 close to Leitrim Village at around twenty-past-eleven this morning. Motorists are being advised that the road is currently closed at Drumheckil at the junction of the R280/R209. item.title: Funding announced for refurbishment of Girl Guides Den in Castlerea
item.description: €115,000 worth of funding has been announced for the refurbishment of the Girl Guides Den in Castlerea. The funding has been allocated by the Department of Culture and is match funded by Roscommon County Council. The building based in Somers Park, is set to be transformed into an arts space for the community. Local Councillor Paschal Fitzmaurice has welcomed the funding announcement: Advertisement

item.title: Calls for adequate staffing to cover home help hours in South Leitrim
item.description: Calls have been in south Leitrim to ensure enough staff are in place to cover allocated home help hours. The service is described as essential for elderly and disabled people across local communities. However, concerns are growing about ongoing staffing shortages in the south of the county. Local Cllr Róisín Kenny is calling on the local authority to contact the HSE on the matter. The Sinn Féin representative says the role of the home help cannot be understated: Advertisement

item.title: Hopes new running track in Roscommon will open in next 2-3 years
item.description: A local athletics club chairman is hopeful the proposed 400m eight lane running track in Roscommon Town will open in the next 2-3 years. Roscommon AC chairman Paul McNamara says the track will massively benefit young athletes in the region. item.title: Boost for Dingle ahead of All Ireland Senior club final
item.description: Dingle have received a boost ahead of Sunday's week's All-Ireland club football final against St Brigid's. AFL side Geelong have given the go ahead to Mark O'Connor to play in the match for his home club. The midfielder - who played a key role in the semi-final win over Ballyboden St Enda's - will then return to pre-season in Australia. item.title: Patrick Smyth
item.description: Patrick Smyth Drumdarton, Aughnasheelin, Co. Leitrim and London, England. Patrick Smyth died on 12 December 2025. A Life Remembered Patrick Smyth was born on 2 January 1953 in Aughnasheelin, County Leitrim, one of the youngest of nine children of Francie and Margaret Smyth of Drumdarton. Raised in a home rich in faith, family, humour, and closeness, Patrick carried the spirit of Leitrim with him wherever life took him. item.title: Emergency services attend two vehicle crash in Boyle
item.description: Emergency services are currently at the scene of a two vehicle crash in Boyle. The collision, involving a car and a minibus, occurred at Military Road shortly after 4:00pm. Gardaí say no injuries are being reported at this time. Motorists in the area are advised to be expect some delays. Advertisement

item.title: Leitrim Councillor Repeats Call for Early Morning Longford to Sligo Train
item.description: A Leitrim Councillor has repeated his call for a new early morning train service from Longford to Sligo. Fianna Fáil's Sean McGowan is bringing forward a motion to next week's council meeting. He believes there's a demand for a new service which would serve stations in the Shannonside region.
